- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often underestimates the reversal — increase forecast mid-range by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven mean reversion.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon — apply a 3–5% upward bias to early forecast points if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.2 to -0.3), model tends to ignore them — add a small upward adjustment (1–3%) to counteract sentiment-induced mean reversion bias.
